ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correct pair: '___ tall boy and ___ old woman.' (1 mark)
   A. An, an
   B. The, an
   C. A, an
   D. An, a

2. Articles: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya is beautiful.
   B. A Kenya is beautiful.
   C. The Kenya is beautiful.
   D. An Kenya is beautiful.

3. How would you write 9 January 2016 as day, month and year? (1 mark)
   A. 01/09/2016
   B. 9-2016
   C. 09/01/2016
   D. 2016/01/09 only

4. Which is a good way to make a story interesting? (1 mark)
   A. Leave out the ending
   B. Copy a friend
   C. Add small details and one simile
   D. Write very short words

5. Which sentence uses 'a lot of' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. There are a lot of children in the yard.
   B. There are alot of children in the yard.
   C. There are lot of children in the yard.
   D. There are a lot children in the yard.

6. Which word has a silent b? (1 mark)
   A. bat
   B. ribbon
   C. lamb
   D. table

7. Complete: 'This bag is mine and that bag is ___.' (belonging to you) (1 mark)
   A. yours
   B. your
   C. you
   D. yourself

8. Which sentence would be best in the body of a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. I hope you are well.
   B. To whom it may concern
   C. Sincerely, the Manager
   D. Yours faithfully

9. Independent reading means (1 mark)
   A. copying sentences
   B. reading aloud to the class only
   C. reading only for exams
   D. reading on your own without being told what to read

10. What is the comparative of 'happy'? (1 mark)
   A. more happy
   B. happyer
   C. happier
   D. happiest

11. Which is a rule for staying safe on the internet? (1 mark)
   A. Use it with a parent or teacher
   B. Tell everyone your password
   C. Share your address
   D. Open messages from strangers

12. Intonation: Which word has the long sound /uː/? (1 mark)
   A. put
   B. full
   C. computer
   D. good

13. 'A lot of' can be used with (1 mark)
   A. only plural nouns
   B. only names
   C. only verbs
   D. both countable and uncountable nouns

14. Which is a polite offer? (1 mark)
   A. You would like a lot tea?
   B. Would you like much tea bags?
   C. Would you like many tea?
   D. Would you like some tea?

15. In the five-finger test, what does it mean if you use all five fingers on one page? (1 mark)
   A. The book has good pictures
   B. The book is too easy
   C. The book is just right
   D. The book is probably too hard for now

16. How should the initials of Peter Otieno Juma be written? (1 mark)
   A. p.o.juma
   B. P. O. Juma
   C. P O Juma,
   D. p, o, Juma

17. Which is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We climbed Mount Elgon.
   B. We climbed mount elgon,
   C. we climbed mount elgon!
   D. we climbed mount elgon

18. Which is the correct negative of 'We planted beans'? (1 mark)
   A. We didn't plant beans.
   B. We not planted beans.
   C. We didn't planted beans.
   D. We don't planted beans.

19. What is the short form of 'let us'? (1 mark)
   A. le'ts
   B. let'us
   C. let's
   D. lets'

20. Which word in the story means 'said no to doing something'? (1 mark)
   A. noticed
   B. refused
   C. smiled
   D. nodded

21. What does 'customer' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A person who buys something or uses a service
   B. A doctor
   C. A person who sells goods
   D. A teacher

22. Which word is an adverb of manner? (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. carefully
   C. tomorrow
   D. outside

23. What should a person with diarrhoea do? (1 mark)
   A. Stop drinking water
   B. Drink plenty of safe water and see a health worker
   C. Share their cup
   D. Stay away from clean water

24. Which sentence uses 'nor' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   B. She has no soap, nor she does have water.
   C. She has no soap, nor water has she.
   D. She has no soap nor does have water she.

25. What is the full set of coordinating conjunctions? (1 mark)
   A. in, on, at, by, to, from, with
   B. he, she, it, we, you, they, I
   C. for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   D. if, when, while, since, until, unless, after

26. Why should you not click on strange pop-up advertisements? (1 mark)
   A. They improve your reading
   B. They are required by the teacher
   C. They are always free prizes
   D. They may be unsafe

27. Which word begins with the cluster 'cl'? (1 mark)
   A. brush
   B. print
   C. clean
   D. green

28. Which is a factual question about the passage? (1 mark)
   A. What kind of person is Kamau?
   B. Why do you think the head teacher smiled?
   C. What job did Class Six do?
   D. Was the clean-up a success?

29. What is a fine? (1 mark)
   A. Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   B. A kind of salary
   C. A gift of money
   D. A payment for a service

30. What is the -ing form of 'run'? (1 mark)
   A. running
   B. runing
   C. runnning
   D. runeing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why reading with expression is important. (2 marks)

32. List three things that make handwriting legible. (3 marks)

33. Give two nonverbal cues that show a speaker is confident. (2 marks)

34. Arrange in order: (a) Then she paid. (b) Grace entered the shop. (c) Finally, she went home. (2 marks)

35. Name two things that a good listener does when a story is read aloud. (2 marks)

36. List the five parts of a friendly letter. (3 marks)

37. Write the minimal pairs for: ship, seat, sock. (3 marks)

38. Mark the words you would stress in: 'We must keep our compound clean.' (3 marks)

39. Give the meaning of clan, ancestor and adopt. (3 marks)

40. Explain the meaning of 'tax' and 'fine'. (3 marks)

41. In the passage 'The Purse in the Market', what did the purse contain? (2 marks)

42. List three details that a school library form may ask for. (3 marks)

43. Give two words with /θ/ and two with /ð/. (4 marks)

44. Rewrite with correct capital letters and full stops: 'we visited lake victoria in august' (3 marks)

45. Fill in much or many: (a) How ___ eggs? (b) How ___ sugar? (2 marks)

46. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

47. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Baraka types a message and clicks Send.' (2 marks)

48. Write two minimal pairs for /p/ and /b/. (2 marks)

49. Write the steps you would follow to search for information safely online. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — A, an
   Tall starts with a consonant sound, old starts with a vowel sound.

2. A — Kenya is beautiful.
   We do not use the before most country names.

3. C — 09/01/2016
   Day first, then month, then year.

4. C — Add small details and one simile
   Details and similes help the reader picture the story.

5. A — There are a lot of children in the yard.
   A lot of is written as three words and is followed by a noun.

6. C — lamb
   In lamb the b is not pronounced.

7. A — yours
   Yours is the possessive pronoun for you.

8. A — I hope you are well.
   It is a warm, friendly opening line.

9. D — reading on your own without being told what to read
   You choose and read for yourself.

10. C — happier
   Change y to i and add er.

11. A — Use it with a parent or teacher
   A trusted adult keeps you safe.

12. C — computer
   Computer has /uː/ in its second syllable.

13. D — both countable and uncountable nouns
   For example a lot of books and a lot of rain.

14. D — Would you like some tea?
   We use some in offers.

15. D — The book is probably too hard for now
   Five unknown words on a page suggests the book is too hard.

16. B — P. O. Juma
   Capital initials each followed by a full stop.

17. A — We climbed Mount Elgon.
   The first word and the mountain name need capitals, and a statement ends with a full stop.

18. A — We didn't plant beans.
   After didn't, use the base form plant.

19. C — let's
   The apostrophe replaces the u.

20. B — refused
   Some children refused to play with Omondi.

21. A — A person who buys something or uses a service
   A customer visits a shop or a barber.

22. B — carefully
   'Carefully' tells how something is done.

23. B — Drink plenty of safe water and see a health worker
   Drinking safe water and seeking help is important.

24. A — She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   After 'nor', the helping verb comes before the subject.

25. C — for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   The seven are remembered as FANBOYS.

26. D — They may be unsafe
   Strange links can be unsafe.

27. C — clean
   'Clean' begins with c and l.

28. C — What job did Class Six do?
   The answer is stated in the text.

29. A — Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   Fines punish law breaking.

30. A — running
   Double the n.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: It shows the meaning and feeling of a text and makes listeners understand and enjoy it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning/feeling, 1 mark for the effect on the listener.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters of the correct size, letters sitting on the line, even gaps between letters and words, correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Eye contact and standing straight; a smile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: b, a, c
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for b first and 1 mark for a then c.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker; do not interrupt; think about what you hear; ask a question when the speaker finishes (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Address, date, greeting, body, closing and name (address and date may be given together).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 mark for greeting and body, 1 mark for closing and name.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: ship and sheep (or sip); seat and sheet (or sit); sock and shock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct partner word.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: We must KEEP our COMpound CLEAN. (Important words: keep, compound, clean.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each important word.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clan is a large group of families with the same ancestor. An ancestor is a family member who lived long ago. To adopt is to take a child into your family and raise the child as your own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tax is money paid to the government to help run the country. A fine is money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule or law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for showing a difference.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It had some coins and a card with the name Mrs Achieng Odhiambo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the coins and 1 mark for the card.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, grade, date of birth, school name, address, class teacher, head teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: /θ/: think, three, thank, mouth (any two). /ð/: this, that, the, mother (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: We visited Lake Victoria in August.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for We, 1 mark for Lake Victoria and August, 1 mark for the full stop.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) many (b) much
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is reading quickly to get the main idea; scanning is looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Baraka typed a message and clicked Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each verb.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: pin, bin and pat, bat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what to find out; choose key words; use an approved site; read carefully and note the facts in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.
